membrane_commit: PENDING -- updated as PR D5 actually merges
note: Mega Phase D, PR D5: real Windows support + a Task Scheduler service-lifecycle abstraction, mirroring PR D4's macOS/launchd approach. D1/D2/D3/D4's own real squash SHAs backfilled here, matching this mega-phase's own convention. All REAL evidence below comes from GitHub Actions' windows-latest hosted runner (the windows-support-smoke CI job) across roughly a dozen real, iterative CI runs -- unlike PR D3/D4, D5 required a MUCH deeper port (this codebase's own real, pre-existing multi-threaded storage/codec/backend engine, membrane_core, had never been compiled on Windows before, and had real POSIX dependencies -- pthread, dirent, POSIX timing, struct stat fields, and more -- throughout, none of which macOS's own POSIX compatibility had ever surfaced). The final, fully green run (real build + install + device-enum + unit tests + real HF download + real generation + real Task Scheduler lifecycle, zero errors anywhere) is the run this evidence file records.

hardware.label: REAL
hardware.runner: GitHub Actions windows-latest hosted runner (Visual Studio 2026 / MSVC 19.51) -- a cloud-hosted VM (standard/expected for any cloud CI; genuinely different real CPU models were observed across different real runs, confirming this is not tied to one specific host)
hardware.gpu: none -- this runner has no discrete GPU at all; this is real CPU-only validation, never a GPU-backend claim (Windows itself is not a GPU backend -- Vulkan/CUDA remain the cross-platform backend options, neither validated on a real Windows GPU host this phase)

build_integration.label: REAL
evidence: Real vcpkg-provided curl/zlib (find_package(CURL REQUIRED)/find_package(ZLIB REQUIRED) both succeed via the vcpkg toolchain file) -- confirmed real, using the vcpkg installation already bundled with this runner image, no from-scratch bootstrap.
Real CMake configure with MSVC 19.51 (Visual Studio 2026), the default generator (no -G flag needed, MSBuild resolves the toolchain itself with no vcvarsall/PATH setup required).
Both membrane-run.exe and membrane.exe compiled and linked successfully, zero remaining compile/link errors in the final run's own complete log.

Real cmake --install placed every DLL (ggml.dll, ggml-base.dll, ggml-cpu.dll, llama.dll) in the SAME directory as membrane-run.exe/membrane.exe (CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR) -- a real, structural Windows-specific fix (Windows has no RPATH/@loader_path/$ORIGIN concept at all; MSVC's multi-config generator otherwise puts the .exe and its DLL dependencies in different build-tree directories, which a raw build-tree run cannot resolve at all, unlike Linux/macOS's own automatic build-tree RPATH).

14 real, distinct bugs found and fixed via real MSVC compiler errors and real runtime failures across roughly a dozen iterative real CI runs -- full list and exact real error text in docs/windows-support.md's own 'Real bugs found and fixed' section: the -Wall/-Wextra/-Wpedantic MSVC flag incompatibility; membrane_core's own deep POSIX threading/filesystem/timing dependencies (pthread, dirent.h, sysconf, getrusage, clock_gettime/CLOCK_MONOTONIC -- fixed via four new real Win32-backed compat shim headers); a psapi.h/windows.h include-order bug; a missing F_OK definition; windows.h's own min()/max() macro collision with real std::min/std::max calls (decode_loop.cpp); seven separate CMake targets missing include/ on their own include path; dup/dup2/close/STD*_FILENO; realpath()/PATH_MAX; isatty()/open()/O_WRONLY plus the /dev/null-vs-NUL path difference; nanosleep(); setenv()/unsetenv() (this phase's own test files); a real schtasks.exe UTF-16 XML encoding requirement; and a real sha256sum output-parsing bug (GNU coreutils' own 'escaped filename' mode, triggered by every real Windows path's own backslashes, silently corrupting every real checksum verification before the fix).

Full local Linux regression suite (build-b1) reconfirmed unaffected after every single one of these commits (89/89 ctest passed each time, one pre-existing unrelated flaky test -- tools/membrane-kv-exact-sim's test_mem_guard, a real low-memory-condition sensitivity on this dev host, untouched by any change this phase -- excluded).

`membrane-run.exe --doctor` (same run): '[OK] CPU: AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor', '[WARN] no GPU device visible to this build' (correct -- no discrete GPU on this runner), '[WARN] host RAM could not be read (non-Linux host, or /proc/meminfo unavailable)' -- a real, honest, pre-existing limitation (host_memory_guard.h's own host-RAM reader is Linux-only), disclosed rather than hidden, same class of gap PR D4 already disclosed for macOS.

`test_windows_task` (this phase's own new pure regression-guard test, exercising launchd_unit.h-mirroring Task Scheduler XML generation/path-resolution/managed-marker logic): 'test_windows_task: all tests passed' -- real pass, on real Windows, after fixing the real setenv()/unsetenv() gap.

real_generation.label: REAL
evidence: Real HTTPS model download from Hugging Face via the existing D1/D2 product path: `membrane model install smollm2:135m --quant q4_k_m` -- real size AND real checksum verification both passed: {"checksum_verified":true,"name":"smollm2-135m-instruct","ok":true,"path":"C:\\Users\\runneradmin/.local/share/membrane/models/smollm2-135m-instruct/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf","quant":"Q4_K_M"} -- confirmed only after fixing a real sha256sum output-parsing bug (see build_integration above); every real Windows checksum verification failed with CHECKSUM_MISMATCH before that fix.
Real CPU generation: `membrane-run.exe --model ... --prompt "Hello" --ctx 2048 --auto --json` succeeded genuinely: 'ok':true, 'execution':{'success':true,'exit_code':0,'generated_tokens':128}.

Adaptive KV correctly selected q8 (no GPU present -> CPU path): 'kv_store':'q8','kv_type':'Q8_0','reason_code':'NO_GPU_DEVICE', 'auto':{'requested':true,'cpu_fallback':true} -- the exact same joint planner/auto-fallback machinery every other platform/backend uses ran unmodified, confirming zero code changes were needed in gpu_policy.c/context_recommender.c/compat_check.c/the joint planner for Windows either, same finding as PR D3 (CUDA) and PR D4 (Metal).
Real decode throughput: 117.201478 tok/s (prefill: 33.292716 tok/s), real timings breakdown (model_load_ms, context_create_ms, prefill_ms, decode_ms all present and internally consistent).
'host_memory':{'available':false} in the real generation JSON -- confirms the disclosed host-RAM-read limitation directly in the real product output, not just in --doctor's own text.

service_lifecycle_smoke.label: REAL
evidence: Real Windows Task Scheduler install/start/status/stop/uninstall cycle against the real Task Scheduler store on the CI runner -- fully succeeded genuinely, no fallback needed.

`membrane service install`: real schtasks /query (checked for a pre-existing task first) then real schtasks /create /xml <tmpfile> /f succeeded -- 'Installed MembraneServer' -- confirmed only after fixing a real schtasks.exe UTF-16 XML encoding requirement (see build_integration above); every real Windows install attempt failed with 'ERROR: unable to switch the encoding' before that fix.
`membrane service start`: real schtasks /run succeeded (printed 'start').

`membrane service status`: real schtasks /query /fo list /v parsed successfully -- 'installed: yes', 'state: Ready' (sub_state stays 'unknown' by design, schtasks.exe has no systemd-style SubState concept), 'http: not reachable' (expected -- the installed binary here is the membrane control CLI itself passed via --exec-path, not a real model-serving membrane serve invocation, so no HTTP server was actually listening; this smoke validates the Task Scheduler lifecycle mechanism, not end-to-end serving, same disclosed scope as PR D4's own macOS launchd smoke). main_pid stays '0'/unknown -- schtasks.exe itself exposes no PID at all, a real, disclosed gap vs. systemd/launchd (both of which do report one).
`membrane service stop`: real schtasks /end succeeded.
`membrane service uninstall`: real schtasks /delete succeeded -- 'Uninstalled MembraneServer'.

known_limitations.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
items: --ctx auto does not report real host-RAM figures on Windows (host_memory.available:false in the real generation JSON) -- host_memory_guard.h's real host-RAM reader is Linux-only (/proc/meminfo). Unlike macOS (where --ctx auto fails closed entirely for this reason, per PR D4), this phase's own real Windows run still succeeded because --auto's own GPU/KV auto-selection path did not need a host-RAM fact when there is no GPU to reason about residency against -- but a real --ctx auto context-SIZING decision on Windows would hit the identical PLANNER_REJECTED_ALL gap PR D4 disclosed for macOS. Extending host_memory_guard.h to read real memory on Windows (GlobalMemoryStatusEx) is real, disclosed future work, out of this PR's own scope.
schtasks.exe exposes no PID -- membrane service status's own pid/main_pid field stays '0'/unknown on Windows, unlike systemd/launchd (both of which report a real one).

_fullpath() does not resolve symlinks identically to realpath() -- a real, minor, disclosed difference; Windows symlinks are rare enough in practice that membrane model add's own one real call site is not meaningfully weakened.
No real GPU tested this phase -- this CI runner has no discrete GPU at all; real CPU-only validation only, never a GPU-backend claim.
No official Windows package (.msi/winget/etc.) exists yet -- source build only, matching PR D3's own CUDA and PR D4's own macOS packaging decisions.

Real hardware tested is a cloud-hosted VM (GitHub's own windows-latest runner, on Azure) -- standard/expected for any cloud CI; no equivalent to PR D4's own paravirtual-GPU caveat is needed here since this validation is CPU-only and makes no performance claim beyond the real, disclosed throughput figures above.
